zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Taḥrīm (The Prohibition)
Medinan
﷽
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبِيُّ لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ ما أحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكَ تَبْتَغِي مَرْضاتَ أزْواجِكَ واللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ means: Allah has forgiven you that prohibition. It has come in the exegesis that the Prophet ﷺ drank honey at the house of Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, and ʿĀʾisha and Ḥafṣa agreed to say to him: "We smell on you the odour of maghāfīr." ”اَلْمَغافِيرُ“ is a gum with an altered smell; and it is said in the exegesis that it is a herb. When he came to each of them, she said to him: "I smell on you the odour of maghāfīr." So the Prophet ﷺ forbade himself the drinking of honey; and it is said that he swore to that. And it has come in the exegesis — and this is the more widely held — that the Prophet ﷺ «was alone, on a day belonging to ʿĀʾisha, with his slave-girl, the mother of Ibrāhīm, who was called "Māriya the Copt." Ḥafṣa came upon that, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: "Do not inform ʿĀʾisha of that." She said to him: "I will not." And he forbade Māriya to himself — and it is said that he also swore along with that. Then Ḥafṣa informed ʿĀʾisha of the news and asked her to keep it secret; and Allah acquainted His Prophet with that, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَإذْ أسَرَّ النَّبِيُّ إلى بَعْضِ أزْواجِهِ حَدِيثًا﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 3]», meaning Ḥafṣa. The position of ”إذْ“ is accusative, as though He said: "And remember when the Prophet confided a matter to one of his wives," meaning Ḥafṣa. ﴿فَلَمّا نَبَّأتْ بِهِ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 3] means: when she told ʿĀʾisha of it.

﴿وَأظْهَرَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ وأعْرَضَ عَنْ بَعْضٍ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 3] — it was also read ”عَرَفَ بَعْضَهُ“, with the rāʾ undoubled. And Allah made known that the prohibition, according to this exegesis, does not make (the thing) forbidden, and He said to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ ما أحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكَ تَبْتَغِي مَرْضاتَ أزْواجِكَ﴾. So Allah did not grant His Prophet the right to forbid anything except what Allah has forbidden; and according to both of these exegeses no one may forbid what Allah has made lawful. Then Allah said: ﴿قَدْ فَرَضَ اللَّهُ لَكم تَحِلَّةَ أيْمانِكُمْ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 2], meaning the expiation, because it has been transmitted that he swore along with that prohibition; and some said the expiation is the expiation for the prohibition (itself). As for ﴿عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 3], its interpretation is that he made Ḥafṣa aware of part of it. ﴿وَأعْرَضَ عَنْ بَعْضٍ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 3]: it has come in the exegesis that when he forbade Māriya (to himself), he told Ḥafṣa that after him Abū Bakr and ʿUmar would rule; so he made her aware of part of the news she had divulged and turned away from part. For the Prophet ﷺ had made known everything he had confided [Translator's note: so printed (عَرَّفَ); the argument seems to require "knew" (عَرَفَ)], and turning away can only be from what is known. The interpretation of this in the language is good and clear: the meaning of ﴿عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 3] is "he requited (her) for it," as you say to someone you are threatening: "I know what you did, I am aware of what you have done," its meaning being "so I will requite you for it," not that you intend merely that you know. Like it is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَما تَفْعَلُوا مِن خَيْرٍ يَعْلَمْهُ اللَّهُ﴾ [al-Baqara: 197], whose interpretation is: Allah knows it and requites it — for Allah knows everything that is done. Like it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُ اللَّهُ ما في قُلُوبِهِمْ فَأعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 63], while Allah knows what is in the hearts of all creatures. And like it is His saying: ﴿فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُ﴾ [al-Zalzala: 7]: the point is not that he sees what he did; he only sees the recompense of what he did. It is said that the Prophet ﷺ divorced Ḥafṣa with a single pronouncement, and that was her recompense in his view; that is the interpretation of ﴿عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ وأعْرَضَ عَنْ بَعْضٍ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 3], i.e. he requited (her) for part of the matter. Ḥafṣa was much given to fasting and to standing in prayer at night, so Allah the Exalted commanded him to take her back, and he took her back.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿إنْ تَتُوبا إلى اللَّهِ فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُما﴾ — He means by it ʿĀʾisha and Ḥafṣa. The meaning of ﴿صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُما﴾ is: your hearts have swerved and deviated from truthfulness.

His saying: ﴿وَإنْ تَظاهَرا عَلَيْهِ فَإنَّ اللَّهَ هو مَوْلاهُ﴾ means: (if) you two support one another against him, then Allah is his protector (mawlā), i.e. He undertakes his support. ﴿وَجِبْرِيلُ وصالِحُ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis that "the righteous of the believers" are Abū Bakr and ʿUmar; it has also come in the exegesis that the righteous of the believers is ʿUmar; and it is said that the righteous of the believers are the best of the Muslims. ”صالِحُ“ here stands for the plural, as you say: "The good one among people does this," meaning every good person. ﴿والمَلائِكَةُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ ظَهِيرٌ﴾ — in the sense of ”ظُهَراءُ“ (supporters), i.e. the angels too are helpers of the Prophet ﷺ.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿عَسى رَبُّهُ إنْ طَلَّقَكُنَّ أنْ يُبْدِلَهُ أزْواجًا خَيْرًا مِنكُنَّ مُسْلِماتٍ﴾ — it was also read ”يُبَدِّلَهُ“, with a doubled dāl and a fatḥa on the bāʾ; ”يُبَدِّلَهُ“ is for intensiveness. Both are good, and it has been read so.

His saying: ﴿قانِتاتٍ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis: obedient. ”اَلْقُنُوتُ“ is performing what brings one near to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿سائِحاتٍ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis from the Prophet ﷺ «that the sāʾiḥūn are those who fast», and this is among what is in the earlier scriptures. The lexicographers said: the one fasting was only called ”سائِحٌ“ (a wanderer) because the one who wanders is devoted to worship and has no provisions with him, so when he finds provisions he eats; and the one fasting likewise spends the day without eating anything. Because of his resemblance to him he was called ”سائِحًا“.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قُوا أنْفُسَكم وأهْلِيكم نارًا﴾ means: hold yourselves and your families to what brings one near to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and keep yourselves and your families away from acts of disobedience. The meaning of ﴿قُوا أنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ is: guard (waqqū) yourselves. It has come in the exegesis: "May Allah have mercy on a man who says: 'O my family, your prayer, your fasting, your poor, your orphan, your neighbours!'" — meaning: keep to and preserve your prayer and these things mentioned; fulfil Allah's obligation in them. And in the ḥadīth: «"Perhaps Allah will gather them with him in Paradise."»

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَقُودُها النّاسُ والحِجارَةُ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis that they are stones of sulphur. ”اَلْوَقُودُ“, with a fatḥa on the wāw, is that with which fire is kindled, firewood and the like; one says ”وَقَدْتُ النّارَ، وُقُودًا“ (I kindled the fire), with a ḍamma on the wāw.

zajjaj:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا تُوبُوا إلى اللَّهِ تَوْبَةً نَصُوحًا﴾ — with a fatḥa on the nūn; it is also read ”نُصُوحًا“ with a ḍamma on the nūn. Whoever gives the fatḥa takes it as a naʿt (adjective) of the repentance, meaning "a repentance consummate in sincerity"; ”فَعُولٌ“ is one of the agent forms used for intensiveness in description: you say "a man patient (ṣabūr) and grateful (shakūr)" and "a sincere repentance (tawba naṣūḥ)." Whoever read ”نُصُوحًا“ with a ḍamma on the nūn, its meaning is "they are sincere in this with sincerity (nuṣūḥ)"; one says ”نَصَحْتُ لَهُ نُصْحًا، ونِصاحَةً، ونُصُوحًا“ (I was sincere to him).

It has come in the exegesis that the sincere repentance is that after which the penitent does not return to the sin; and some of them said: that with which he does not intend to return to the sin.

His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ لا يُخْزِي اللَّهُ النَّبِيَّ والَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ﴾ — ”يَوْمَ“ is accusative through His saying: ﴿عَسى رَبُّكم أنْ يُكَفِّرَ عَنْكم سَيِّئاتِكم ويُدْخِلَكم جَنّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِها الأنْهارُ يَوْمَ لا يُخْزِي اللَّهُ النَّبِيَّ﴾, i.e. on that day. The reading is the accusative in His saying ﴿وَيُدْخِلَكُمْ﴾, conjoined to ﴿أنْ يُكَفِّرَ﴾; had it been read with the jussive, that would be a valid way, construed on the position of ﴿عَسى رَبُّكم أنْ يُكَفِّرَ عَنْكم سَيِّئاتِكُمْ﴾, because ”عَسى“ from Allah is binding. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَإنِّي لَغَفّارٌ لِمَن تابَ وآمَنَ وعَمِلَ صالِحًا ثُمَّ اهْتَدى﴾ [Ṭāhā: 82]. And His saying: ﴿نُورُهم يَسْعى بَيْنَ أيْدِيهِمْ وبِأيْمانِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنا أتْمِمْ لَنا نُورَنا﴾ means: when the believers see the light of the hypocrites being extinguished, they ask Allah to perfect their light for them.

zajjaj:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلا لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا امْرَأتَ نُوحٍ وامْرَأتَ لُوطٍ كانَتا تَحْتَ عَبْدَيْنِ مِن عِبادِنا صالِحَيْنِ فَخانَتاهُما فَلَمْ يُغْنِيا عَنْهُما مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا﴾ — Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that the prophets avail nothing for one who commits acts of disobedience. It has come in the exegesis that their betrayal was not in harlotry, because Allah does not afflict the prophets with corruption in their wives. It is said that the betrayal of Lūṭ's wife was that she used to point out the guests, and the betrayal of Nūḥ's wife was that she used to say he was mad — Allah bless him and all His prophets. Whoever claims otherwise is mistaken; for some of those who interpreted His saying ﴿يا نُوحُ إنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِن أهْلِكَ إنَّهُ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صالِحٍ﴾ [Hūd: 46] inclined to a kind of corruption. The reading here is ”عَمِلَ غَيْرَ صالِحٍ“ and ﴿عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صالِحٍ﴾ [Hūd: 46], and both come back to one meaning: the interpretation of ﴿إنَّهُ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صالِحٍ﴾ [Hūd: 46] is "he is one of unrighteous deeds." Whoever disbelieves, his kinship with his believing family is cut off: he does not inherit from them, nor do they inherit from him.

zajjaj:11-11.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا امْرَأتَ فِرْعَوْنَ إذْ قالَتْ رَبِّ ابْنِ لِي عِنْدَكَ بَيْتًا في الجَنَّةِ ونَجِّنِي مِن فِرْعَوْنَ وعَمَلِهِ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis that Pharaoh drove four stakes for her, bound her body and her legs, placed a millstone on her chest and put her in the sun; and that Allah gave her relief, and she saw her house in Paradise. It has also come in the exegesis that the angels used to shade her from the sun with their wings.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَرْيَمَ ابْنَتَ عِمْرانَ الَّتِي أحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَها فَنَفَخْنا فِيهِ مِن رُوحِنا وصَدَّقَتْ بِكَلِماتِ رَبِّها وكُتُبِهِ﴾ — it was also read ”وَكِتابِهِ“. ﴿أحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَها﴾: it has come in the exegesis that what is meant by it is the opening of her garment. The Arabs say of a chaste man: "He is clean of garment" and "He is good of waistband (ḥujza)," meaning that he is chaste. They recited the verse of al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī:
؎رِقاقُ النِّعالِ طَيِّبٌ حُجُزاتُهم ∗∗∗ يُحَيُّونَ بِالرَّيْحانِ يَوْمَ السَّباسِبِ
(Fine of sandals, good of waistbands, they are greeted with sweet basil on the day of al-Sabāsib.)
They explained ”طَيِّبٌ حُجُزاتُهُمْ“ as meaning that they are chaste. Likewise ﴿فَنَفَخْنا فِيهِ مِن رُوحِنا﴾ means: into the opening of her garment.
